decisions.question: Are page open/close and annotation visibility events distinct where the layout shows multiple pages?
decisions.verdict: ADR 2814 superseded the one-page-only premise for non-script event dispatch. Current TwoPageLeft tests prove page 1 can become visible while page 0 remains current. Retain the page's O/C versus annotation PO/PC distinction and the arrangement-based PV/PI dispatch for non-script actions. Do not repeat B22's catalog-action ordering finding.

decisions.question: May annotation PV/PI JavaScript be delayed until the page becomes current, by coalescing it with PO/PC?
evidence: ISO 32000-2 EC3 Table 197 physical 523 / printed 508 says PV action shall be performed when page becomes visible and PI when no longer visible; §12.6.3 physical 522 / printed 507 says the pair distinguishes visible pages from open pages.
A286/ADR 1904 makes in-document/in-viewer script effects supported when a runner is enabled; scripts are off by default under A193/ADR 1616.

viewer/navigation.rs dispatches non-script PV/PI at arrangement diffs; script_sites.rs::annotation_triggers associates PageOpen with PO+PV and PageClose with PC+PI; pointer.rs suppresses JavaScript refusal as 'handed over' for visibility events without calling run_annotation_scripts.
decisions.verdict: Reconsider the accepted delay for enabled scripts in a multi-page layout. Table 197 has no exception for JavaScript actions, and delaying the visible-neighbor's script until it becomes current means the script is not run at its Table 197 trigger. Engine-off remains an explicit reader policy and is not the concern. A recording-runner test of the existing viewer callback is the right discriminator; it makes no engine claim.
decisions.status: Candidate source/implementation mismatch pending parent interpretation and execution of supplied draft.

decisions.question: Are scripts handed to the runner at their event site, including visibility events?
decisions.verdict: Pointer/focus events and page O/C sites are exercised; ADR's claim that page scripts are raised with open/close does not establish a multi-page PV/PI callback at the visibility transition. The supplied test isolates this boundary.

decisions.question: Does the script exclusion prevent the proposed test or make this a policy departure?
decisions.verdict: No. The enabled in-document/viewer runner path is within the accepted scope; the default Off and the absence of an interpreter in the test are not conflated with skipping the event dispatch when Run supplies a runner. No test asserts arbitrary script semantics.

decisions.question: Is this the same AA inheritance defect as terminal-field K?
decisions.verdict: No. B62 concerns field ancestor inheritance; this candidate has annotation-local AA on distinct pages and tests when an already-resolved action is delivered.
